page.overview:
Who is Sauron?

Sauron (Quenya; or Vanyarin|), the eponymous Lord of the Rings, was the greatest fallen Maia, a former renowned disciple of Aulë, the chief agent of the first Dark Lord Morgoth in the Elder Days (First Age), the second Dark Lord, the maker of the One Ring, and self-proclaimed ruler of Middle-earth in the Second Age and near the end of the Third Age.

In the Days before days, Sauron was corrupted by Melkor (later named Morgoth) to betray the Valar and serve him. He served as Morgoth's chief lieutenant throughout the First Age. After Morgoth's ousting by the Valar at the end of the First Age, Sauron went into hiding out of pride and shame. To the Sindar of Beleriand, Sauron was known as Gorthaur in the First Age.

Sauron returned to Middle-earth about 500 years into the Second Age, becoming the second Dark Lord and plotting to conquer Middle-earth as his former master had. After deceiving the Elves into making the Rings of Power, Sauron deceitfully forged the One Ring with the intent to use it to dominate the wills of the Elven lords who wore the other Rings. In this way, he hoped to dominate the Elves and ultimately bring them, and the rest of Middle-earth, under his dominion. The plan failed, however, and Sauron would go on to wage a lengthy, but ultimately fruitless, war against the Elves and Númenóreans. Defeated, Sauron returned to Mordor to rebuild his forces, and the world knew peace for a time.

Sauron would eventually grow in might once more, but his pride and vanity attracted the attention of the Númenóreans once again. By the end of the Second Age, they had become so powerful that even Sauron could not hope to overcome them militarily, and they journeyed to Mordor to force Sauron to swear fealty. Sauron acknowledged the overwhelming might of the Númenóreans and traveled back with them to their island homeland as a hostage. There, however, Sauron caused the Downfall of Númenor through cunning manipulation and deception, yet was eventually defeated once more during the War of the Last Alliance of Elves and Men united under Gil-galad and Elendil at the end of the Second Age. In the final battle, Isildur cut the One Ring from Sauron's hand, destroying his corporeal form and robbing him of much of his power.

Also known as: Dark Lord.
